claims.claim: Treatment with the DNMT inhibitor decitabine restored CDO1 mRNA expression in NSCLC cell lines.
claims.source: CDO1 protein expression was undetectable in a panel of NSCLC cell lines with the exception of H1581 cells (Figure 3C), and treatment with the DNMT inhibitor decitabine restored CDO1 mRNA expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: CDO1 is epigenetically silenced by promoter methylation in NSCLC cell lines and patient samples.
claims.source: These results indicate that CDO1 epigenetically silenced by promoter methylation in NSCLC cell lines and patient samples.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the TCGA data and cell line experiments.

claims.claim: CDO1 accumulated to higher levels in NRF2HIGH cells than NRF2LOW.
claims.source: We find that CDO1 accumulated to higher levels in NRF2HIGH cells than NRF2LOW, although accumulation was observed in many NRF2LOW cell lines as well (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: There is a strong association between the level of CDO1 accumulation and intracellular CYS levels across the panel of parental cell lines.
claims.source: We investigated the association with intracellular CYS levels across the panel of parental cell lines and found a strong association between the level of CDO1 accumulation and intracellular CYS levels but not with the level of CDO1 mRNA expressed from our inducible promoter system (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), which is consistent with our findings in Keap1R554Q MEFs (Figure 2A,B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: There is no association between CDO1 accumulation and the level of CDO1 mRNA expressed from the inducible promoter system.
claims.source: We investigated the association with intracellular CYS levels across the panel of parental cell lines and found a strong association between the level of CDO1 accumulation and intracellular CYS levels but not with the level of CDO1 mRNA expressed from our inducible promoter system (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), which is consistent with our findings in Keap1R554Q MEFs (Figure 2A,B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: NRF2 promoted CSA accumulation and (CYS)2 consumption following CDO1WT expression in NRF2 KO cells.
claims.source: NRF2 promoted CSA accumulation and (CYS)2 consumption following CDO1WT expression in NRF2 KO cells (Figure 4G,H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 4G and 4H.

claims.claim: NRF2T80K expression in KEAP1WT cells promoted CSA accumulation and (CYS)2 consumption following CDO1WT expression.
claims.source: This effect was recapitulated by NRF2T80K expression in KEAP1WT cells (Figure 4I,J).
claims.evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 4I and 4J.

claims.claim: NRF2 depletion by KEAP1WT expression in KEAP1MUT cells inhibited the CDO1-dependent production of CSA.
claims.source: Consistently, NRF2 depletion by KEAP1WT expression in KEAP1MUT cells inhibited the CDO1-dependent production of CSA (Figure 4K–M).
claims.evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 4K-M.

claims.claim: Intracellular CYS can influence CDO1 activity promoting its catalytic efficiency.
claims.source: Intracellular CYS can also influence CDO1 activity promoting its catalytic efficiency (Dominy et al., 2008), which may explain these results.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: CDO1 expression promotes the production of CSA from CYS, leading to CSA accumulation both intracellularly and extracellularly, and enhanced (CYS)2 consumption.
claims.source: Collectively, these results demonstrate that CDO1 expression promotes the production of CSA from CYS, leading to CSA accumulation both intracellularly and extracellularly, and enhanced (CYS)2 consumption.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data in Figure 4.

claims.claim: Significant accumulation of SO32- was found in CDO1-expressing cells.
claims.source: To further characterize the consequence of CDO1 expression on CYS metabolism, we performed untargeted metabolomics and found significant accumulation of SO32- in CDO1-expressing cells (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by untargeted metabolomics data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: CSA can be transaminated by the cytosolic aspartate aminotransferase (GOT1) to produce β-sulfinyl pyruvate, which spontaneously decomposes to pyruvate and SO32-.
claims.source: Importantly, CSA can be transaminated by the cytosolic aspartate aminotransferase (GOT1) to produce β-sulfinyl pyruvate, which spontaneously decomposes to pyruvate and SO32- (Singer and Kearney, 1956) (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: SO32- is toxic at high levels due to its cleavage of disulfide bonds in proteins and small molecules, including (CYS)2.
claims.source: While HTAU and TAU are non-toxic molecules that have important physiological functions (Aruoma et al., 1988; Hansen et al., 2010; Schaffer et al., 2000; Suzuki et al., 2002), SO32- is toxic at high levels due to its cleavage of disulfide bonds in proteins and small molecules, including (CYS)2 (Clarke, 1932).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: SO32- production may contribute to (CYS)2 depletion through disulfide cleavage, also known as sulfitolysis.
claims.source: Thus, we hypothesized that in addition to accounting for the fate of CSA metabolism, SO32- production may also contribute to (CYS)2 depletion through disulfide cleavage, also known as sulfitolysis.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental observations.

claims.claim: CDO1WT-, but not CDO1Y157F-expressing A549s demonstrated rapid accumulation of extracellular SO32- over the 24 hr time course following media replenishment.
claims.source: We next performed a quantitative analysis of SO32- levels following CDO1 expression. CDO1WT-, but not CDO1Y157F-expressing A549s demonstrated rapid accumulation of extracellular SO32- over the 24 hr time course following media replenishment (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: The accumulation of the product of the sulfitolysis reaction, cysteine-S-sulfate (CYS-SO3-), was observed in the medium of CDO1WT-expressing cells.
claims.source: Further, the accumulation of the product of the sulfitolysis reaction, cysteine-S-sulfate (CYS-SO3-), was also observed in the medium of CDO1WT-expressing cells (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: CYS-SO3- appeared earlier than SO32-, and stopped accumulating once (CYS)2 levels were depleted.
claims.source: We observed that CYS-SO3- appeared earlier than SO32-, and stopped accumulating once (CYS)2 levels were depleted, suggesting that SO32- reacted with (CYS)2 in a rapid and complete manner.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the time course data.

claims.claim: SO32- reacted with (CYS)2 in a rapid and complete manner.
claims.source: We observed that CYS-SO3- appeared earlier than SO32-, and stopped accumulating once (CYS)2 levels were depleted, suggesting that SO32- reacted with (CYS)2 in a rapid and complete manner.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the time course data.

claims.claim: Incubation of sodium sulfite (Na2SO3) with culture medium in the absence of cells resulted in rapid and robust conversion of (CYS)2 to CYS-SO3- within 5 min.
claims.source: To test this possibility, we incubated either CSA or sodium sulfite (Na2SO3) with culture medium in the absence of cells, and observed rapid and robust conversion of (CYS)2 to CYS-SO3- by Na2SO3 (Figure 5E), but not CSA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), within 5 min.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: CSA did not convert (CYS)2 to CYS-SO3- when incubated with culture medium in the absence of cells.
claims.source: To test this possibility, we incubated either CSA or sodium sulfite (Na2SO3) with culture medium in the absence of cells, and observed rapid and robust conversion of (CYS)2 to CYS-SO3- by Na2SO3 (Figure 5E), but not CSA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), within 5 min.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Similar depletion kinetics could be observed by substituting (CYS)2 with oxidized glutathione (GSSG) in the sulfitolysis reaction.
claims.source: Interestingly, similar depletion kinetics in this experiment could also be observed by substituting (CYS)2 with oxidized glutathione (GSSG) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D), although intracellular and extracellular levels of GSSG in cell culture were much lower than (CYS)2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E,F), suggesting it is not the major target of SO32-.
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D.

claims.claim: Intracellular and extracellular levels of GSSG in cell culture were much lower than (CYS)2, suggesting GSSG is not the major target of SO32-.
claims.source: Interestingly, similar depletion kinetics in this experiment could also be observed by substituting (CYS)2 with oxidized glutathione (GSSG) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D), although intracellular and extracellular levels of GSSG in cell culture were much lower than (CYS)2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E,F), suggesting it is not the major target of SO32-.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E,F.

claims.claim: SO32- is generated downstream of CDO1 and rapidly reacts with (CYS)2, thereby depleting (CYS)2 from the culture media.
claims.source: These results demonstrate that SO32- is generated downstream of CDO1 and rapidly reacts with (CYS)2, thereby depleting (CYS)2 from the culture media.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data in Figure 5.

claims.claim: Deletion of endogenous CDO1 in H1581 cells resulted in a dramatic reduction in CYS-SO3- production.
claims.source: Importantly, deletion of endogenous CDO1 in H1581 cells resulted in a dramatic reduction in CYS-SO3- production (Figure 5F), thereby demonstrating that SO32- is generated by CDO1 under physiological expression levels in lung cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: SO32- is generated by CDO1 under physiological expression levels in lung cells.
claims.source: Importantly, deletion of endogenous CDO1 in H1581 cells resulted in a dramatic reduction in CYS-SO3- production (Figure 5F), thereby demonstrating that SO32- is generated by CDO1 under physiological expression levels in lung cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: NRF2 promoted CYS-SO3- production following CDO1WT expression.

NRF2 promoted CYS-SO3- production following CDO1WT expression (Figure 5G), which was accompanied by significant accumulation of both intracellular and extracellular SO32- (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B,C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 5G.

claims.claim: NRF2 promoted accumulation of both intracellular and extracellular SO32- following CDO1WT expression.
claims.source: To examine the NRF2-dependence of (CYS)2 depletion via SO32-, we utilized the NRF2 KO cells, KEAP1WT, and KEAP1MUT cell lines. NRF2 promoted CYS-SO3- production following CDO1WT expression (Figure 5G), which was accompanied by significant accumulation of both intracellular and extracellular SO32- (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B,C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3B,C.

claims.claim: NRF2 stabilization with β-lapachone promoted CDO1-dependent CSA and CYS-SO3- production and (CYS)2 depletion in H1299 and H1975 cells.
claims.source: Further, NRF2 stabilization with β-lapachone promoted CDO1-dependent CSA and CYS-SO3- production and (CYS)2 depletion in H1299 and H1975 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 3H–J).
claims.evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3H-J.

claims.claim: NRF2 induces CDO1-mediated sulfitolysis, thereby depleting extracellular (CYS)2 in NSCLC cells.
claims.source: Collectively, these results suggest that NRF2 induces CDO1-mediated sulfitolysis, thereby depleting extracellular (CYS)2 in NSCLC cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data in Figure 5.

claims.claim: Treatment of cells with CSA and Na2SO3, but not HTAU, led to cytotoxicity.
claims.source: Next, we examined the toxicity of CDO1 products to NSCLC cell lines. Treatment of cells with CSA and Na2SO3, but not HTAU, led to cytotoxicity (Figure 5—figure supplement 4A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cell viability data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4A.

claims.claim: (CYS)2 starvation and Na2SO3 treatment were universally toxic to NSCLC cell lines, which did not depend on NRF2 activity.
claims.source: We found that (CYS)2 starvation and Na2SO3 treatment were universally toxic to NSCLC cell lines, which did not depend on NRF2 activity (Figure 5—figure supplement 4B,C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cell viability data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4B,C.

claims.claim: CDO1, CSA and Na2SO3 sensitized A549 cells to oxidative stress.
claims.source: In addition, CDO1, CSA and Na2SO3 sensitized A549 cells to oxidative stress (Figure 5—figure supplement 4D,E), consistent with their ability to deplete (CYS)2.
claims.evidence: This is supported by cell viability data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4D,E.

claims.claim: CSA and SO32- are toxic to NSCLC cells regardless of NRF2 activity.
claims.source: Collectively, these results demonstrate that CSA and SO32- are toxic to NSCLC cells regardless of NRF2 activity, suggesting that resistance to (CYS)2 starvation is not an inherent phenotype of NRF2HIGH cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claims.claim: Resistance to (CYS)2 starvation is not an inherent phenotype of NRF2HIGH cells.
claims.source: Collectively, these results demonstrate that CSA and SO32- are toxic to NSCLC cells regardless of NRF2 activity, suggesting that resistance to (CYS)2 starvation is not an inherent phenotype of NRF2HIGH cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data.

claims.claim: NRF2HIGH cells are sensitive to CDO1 expression due to high intracellular CYS and CDO1 stabilization.
claims.source: Rather, they are sensitive to CDO1 expression due to high intracellular CYS and CDO1 stabilization.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claims.claim: GOT1 KO cells had significantly lower CDO1-dependent (CYS)2 consumption and SO32- and CYS-SO3- production rates compared to each parental line.
claims.source: In support of GOT1 mediating the production of SO32- and (CYS)2 depletion, GOT1 KO cells had significantly lower CDO1-dependent (CYS)2 consumption and SO32- and CYS-SO3- production rates compared to each parental line, which was rescued by GOT1 restoration (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: GOT1 restoration rescued the reduced CDO1-dependent (CYS)2 consumption and SO32- and CYS-SO3- production rates in GOT1 KO cells.
claims.source: In support of GOT1 mediating the production of SO32- and (CYS)2 depletion, GOT1 KO cells had significantly lower CDO1-dependent (CYS)2 consumption and SO32- and CYS-SO3- production rates compared to each parental line, which was rescued by GOT1 restoration (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: CDO1 antagonized cell proliferation independent of GOT1 expression and sulfitolysis.
claims.source: Surprisingly, we observed that CDO1 antagonized cell proliferation independent of GOT1 expression and sulfitolysis, suggesting that the intracellular metabolism of CYS also contributes to the phenotype (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by proliferation data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: The intracellular metabolism of CYS contributes to the CDO1-dependent proliferation phenotype.
claims.source: Surprisingly, we observed that CDO1 antagonized cell proliferation independent of GOT1 expression and sulfitolysis, suggesting that the intracellular metabolism of CYS also contributes to the phenotype (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: CDO1 expression did not affect CYS utilization as the rates of GSH, Coenzyme A (CoA), and protein synthesis were similar in NSCLC cell lines.
claims.source: However, unlike in MEFs, CDO1 expression did not affect CYS utilization as the rates of GSH, Coenzyme A (CoA), and protein synthesis were similar (Figure 6D–G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by isotope tracing and protein synthesis data shown in Figure 6D-G.

claims.claim: The NADPH/NADP+ ratio was lower following CDO1 expression in both GOT1 KO and GOT1 expressing cells.
claims.source: Indeed, we observed that the NADPH/NADP+ ratio was lower following CDO1 expression in both GOT1 KO and GOT1 expressing cells (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by NADPH/NADP+ ratio measurements shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: (CYS)2 starvation increased the NADPH/NADP+ ratio.
claims.source: Consistently, (CYS)2 starvation had the opposite effect on the NADPH/NADP+ ratio, which increased following starvation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by NADPH/NADP+ ratio measurements shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The decrease in the NADPH/NADP+ ratio did not dramatically influence the levels of GSH and GSSG in non-stressed cells.
claims.source: While we found that the decrease in the NADPH/NADP+ ratio did not dramatically influence the levels of GSH and GSSG in non-stressed cells (Figure 7B), expression of CDO1 increased sensitivity to the lipid peroxidation inducer cumene hydroperoxide (CuH2O2) independent of GOT1 expression (Figure 7C), and CDO1 deletion in H1581 cells promoted CuH2O2 resistance (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: Expression of CDO1 increased sensitivity to the lipid peroxidation inducer cumene hydroperoxide (CuH2O2) independent of GOT1 expression.
claims.source: While we found that the decrease in the NADPH/NADP+ ratio did not dramatically influence the levels of GSH and GSSG in non-stressed cells (Figure 7B), expression of CDO1 increased sensitivity to the lipid peroxidation inducer cumene hydroperoxide (CuH2O2) independent of GOT1 expression (Figure 7C), and CDO1 deletion in H1581 cells promoted CuH2O2 resistance (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cell viability data shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: CDO1 deletion in H1581 cells promoted CuH2O2 resistance.
claims.source: While we found that the decrease in the NADPH/NADP+ ratio did not dramatically influence the levels of GSH and GSSG in non-stressed cells (Figure 7B), expression of CDO1 increased sensitivity to the lipid peroxidation inducer cumene hydroperoxide (CuH2O2) independent of GOT1 expression (Figure 7C), and CDO1 deletion in H1581 cells promoted CuH2O2 resistance (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cell viability data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: CDO1 expression significantly impaired the ability of NSCLC cell lines to grow in soft agar.
claims.source: Next, we placed cells into detached conditions, which has been shown to increase reliance on IDH1-dependent reductive carboxylation to promote NADPH generation in the mitochondria (Jiang et al., 2016). Consistently, CDO1 expression significantly impaired the ability of NSCLC cell lines to grow in soft agar (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by soft agar assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: CDO1 impaired NADPH-dependent synthesis of proline from glutamate.
claims.source: Using 13C5-glutamine tracing, we observed that glutamine readily entered the TCA cycle to produce M + 4 citrate, which was unaffected or increased following CDO1 expression (Figure 7E,F), but CDO1 impaired both NADPH-dependent synthesis of proline from glutamate (Figure 7D), and NADPH-dependent reductive carboxylation of α-ketoglutarate to produce M + 5 citrate (Figure 7E,F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by isotope tracing data shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: CDO1 impaired NADPH-dependent reductive carboxylation of α-ketoglutarate to produce M + 5 citrate.
claims.source: Using 13C5-glutamine tracing, we observed that glutamine readily entered the TCA cycle to produce M + 4 citrate, which was unaffected or increased following CDO1 expression (Figure 7E,F), but CDO1 impaired both NADPH-dependent synthesis of proline from glutamate (Figure 7D), and NADPH-dependent reductive carboxylation of α-ketoglutarate to produce M + 5 citrate (Figure 7E,F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by isotope tracing data shown in Figure 7E,F.

claims.claim: The antiproliferative effects of CDO1 were CYS-dependent.
claims.source: The antiproliferative effects of CDO1 were CYS-dependent, as either inhibition of (CYS)2 uptake with erastin or low (CYS)2 conditions resulted in loss of CDO1 expression and completely rescued the CDO1-induced proliferation defect (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D–F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by proliferation data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D-F.

claims.claim: Inhibition of (CYS)2 uptake with erastin or low (CYS)2 conditions resulted in loss of CDO1 expression and completely rescued the CDO1-induced proliferation defect.
claims.source: The antiproliferative effects of CDO1 were CYS-dependent, as either inhibition of (CYS)2 uptake with erastin or low (CYS)2 conditions resulted in loss of CDO1 expression and completely rescued the CDO1-induced proliferation defect (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D–F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by proliferation data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D-F.

claims.claim: CDO1 inhibits cellular processes by limiting NADPH availability, thereby impairing cellular proliferation.
claims.source: Collectively, these results suggest that CDO1 further inhibits cellular processes by limiting NADPH availability, thereby impairing cellular proliferation.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data in Figure 7.

claims.claim: KrasG12D; Trp53flox/flox mice had similar survival regardless of Keap1 mutation status.
claims.source: We found that KrasG12D; Trp53flox/flox mice had similar survival regardless of Keap1 mutation status (Figure 8A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by survival data shown in Figure 8A.

claims.claim: KrasG12D; Trp53flox/flox; Keap1R554Q/R554Q mice displayed significant lung hemorrhage at endpoint despite small tumors.
claims.source: However, survival was not related to tumor burden, as KrasG12D; Trp53flox/flox; Keap1R554Q/R554Q mice displayed significant lung hemorrhage at endpoint (Figure 8B) despite small tumors (Figure 8C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by histology data shown in Figure 8B and 8C.

claims.claim: KrasG12D; Trp53flox/flox mice expressing one copy of Keap1R554Q had modestly larger tumors.
claims.source: Quantification of average lung tumor size revealed that KrasG12D; Trp53flox/flox mice expressing one copy of Keap1R554Q had modestly larger tumors, consistent with the findings of Romero et al., and in agreement with the dominant negative activity displayed by select Keap1 mutants (Suzuki et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is supported by tumor size quantification shown in Figure 8C and is consistent with prior literature.

claims.claim: Complete loss of Keap1 function in the Keap1R554Q/R554Q mice led to significantly smaller tumors.

claims.source: Further, Keap1 loss of function led to a gradient of Nrf2 activation with Keap1WT tumors expressing little to no Nqo1, Keap1R554Q/+ tumors displayed increased Nqo1 expression, and Keap1R554Q/R554Q tumors were strongly positive (Figure 8D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8D.

claims.claim: Keap1R554Q/R554Q tumors strongly expressed Cdo1.
claims.source: Importantly, Keap1R554Q/R554Q tumors strongly expressed Cdo1 (Figure 8D), demonstrating that Nrf2 activation promotes Cdo1 accumulation under physiological conditions in vivo, and suggesting that Cdo1 may impede tumor progression.
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8D.

claims.claim: Nrf2 activation promotes Cdo1 accumulation under physiological conditions in vivo.
claims.source: Importantly, Keap1R554Q/R554Q tumors strongly expressed Cdo1 (Figure 8D), demonstrating that Nrf2 activation promotes Cdo1 accumulation under physiological conditions in vivo, and suggesting that Cdo1 may impede tumor progression.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the immunohistochemistry data in Figure 8D.

claims.claim: Cdo1 may impede tumor progression.
claims.source: Importantly, Keap1R554Q/R554Q tumors strongly expressed Cdo1 (Figure 8D), demonstrating that Nrf2 activation promotes Cdo1 accumulation under physiological conditions in vivo, and suggesting that Cdo1 may impede tumor progression.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental data.

claims.source: CDO1 plays a critical role in limiting CYS availability and toxicity (Jurkowska et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.source: CYS promotes both the stability and activity of CDO1 (Stipanuk et al., 2009), leading to the irreversible metabolism of CYS to CSA (Stipanuk et al., 2009).

claims.claim: High intracellular CYS levels are a common feature of lung cancer cell lines.

results.result: NRF2 stabilization in a genetically engineered mouse model (Keap1R554Q) leads to accumulation of intracellular cysteine and sulfur-containing metabolites, particularly those in the taurine biosynthesis pathway (CSA and HTAU), in addition to the expected increase in GSH.
results.evaluation: Claims C27-C34 are well-supported by the generation of the Keap1R554Q mouse model (C27), western blot validation of Nrf2 accumulation (C28), and comprehensive metabolomics data (C29-C34) shown in Figure 1. The quantitative measurements demonstrate millimolar-range increases in HTAU comparable to GSH increases, supporting the conclusion that taurine biosynthesis represents a significant cysteine utilization pathway.

results.result: Nrf2 promotes Cdo1 protein accumulation (without increasing mRNA) in Keap1R554Q MEFs, and Cdo1 mediates cysteine entry into the taurine synthesis pathway while modestly limiting cysteine and GSH accumulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C40 are supported by western blot and qRT-PCR data (C35), isotope tracing experiments with 13C6-cystine (C37, C39), and CRISPR/Cas9 deletion studies (Figure 2). The mechanism of Cdo1 stabilization by cysteine (C36) is established knowledge. The modest effects on GSH are quantitatively demonstrated, though C38 acknowledges incomplete HTAU labeling abolishment with appropriate caveats.

results.result: CDO1 is preferentially silenced by promoter methylation in KEAP1 mutant lung adenocarcinoma compared to wild-type, and this silencing is associated with poor prognosis and confers a selective disadvantage in the context of NRF2 accumulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C51 are well-supported by comprehensive TCGA data analysis (Figure 3A-B, supplements) showing significant associations between CDO1 methylation, expression, KEAP1 mutation status, and patient outcomes. The correlation between methylation and expression (C44) and validation in cell lines with decitabine treatment (C50) strengthen the epigenetic silencing conclusion. The inference of selective disadvantage (C48) is reasonable given the preferential methylation in KEAP1 mutant tumors.

results.result: CDO1 protein accumulation in NSCLC cell lines is strongly associated with intracellular cysteine levels but not with CDO1 mRNA expression from an inducible promoter system.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C54 are supported by western blot analysis across a panel of cell lines (Figure 3D) and correlation analyses (Figure 3D, supplement 2A). The strong correlation with intracellular cysteine (C53) and lack of correlation with mRNA (C54) is consistent with the known post-translational regulation of CDO1 by cysteine, supporting the mechanistic understanding.

results.result: NRF2 promotes CDO1-dependent CSA accumulation and cystine consumption in multiple isogenic NSCLC cell line systems, with intracellular cysteine influencing CDO1 catalytic efficiency.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C61 are supported by metabolomics data from multiple complementary isogenic systems: NRF2 KO/rescue (C57), NRF2T80K expression (C58), and KEAP1 restoration (C59). The data in Figure 4G-M consistently demonstrate NRF2-dependent effects on CSA production and cystine consumption. C60 cites established knowledge about cysteine's effect on CDO1 activity, providing mechanistic context.

results.result: CDO1 expression leads to sulfite (SO32-) production via GOT1-mediated transamination of CSA, and sulfite rapidly depletes cystine through sulfitolysis to produce cysteine-S-sulfate (CYS-SO3-).
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C76 are well-supported by untargeted metabolomics (C62), time-course experiments (C66-C69), cell-free sulfitolysis assays (C70-C73), and endogenous CDO1 deletion studies (C75-C76). The biochemical mechanism (C63) is established knowledge. The rapid kinetics of sulfitolysis and preferential targeting of cystine over GSSG are experimentally demonstrated. The hypothesis (C65) is appropriately labeled as speculation but is subsequently validated experimentally.

results.result: NRF2 promotes CDO1-mediated sulfitolysis and cystine depletion in NSCLC cells, as demonstrated through multiple genetic and pharmacological approaches.
results.evaluation: Claims C77-C80 are supported by metabolomics data from NRF2 KO/rescue experiments (C77-C78, Figure 5G, supplements), and β-lapachone treatment studies (C79, Figure 5 supplement 3H-J). The convergent evidence from genetic and pharmacological NRF2 manipulation strengthens the conclusion that NRF2 drives CDO1-mediated sulfitolysis.

results.result: CSA and sulfite are toxic to NSCLC cells regardless of NRF2 activity, and NRF2HIGH cells are sensitive to CDO1 expression due to high intracellular cysteine and CDO1 stabilization rather than inherent resistance to cystine starvation.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C86 are supported by cell viability assays (Figure 5 supplement 4A-E) showing universal toxicity of CSA and Na2SO3 across NRF2HIGH and NRF2LOW cell lines. The data demonstrate that cystine starvation and sulfite treatment are toxic independent of NRF2 status (C82), supporting the inference that NRF2HIGH cells are sensitive specifically to CDO1 expression due to cysteine accumulation (C86) rather than having inherent resistance (C85).

results.result: GOT1 mediates CDO1-dependent sulfitolysis and cystine depletion, but CDO1 antagonizes cell proliferation independent of GOT1 expression, suggesting intracellular cysteine metabolism also contributes to the antiproliferative phenotype without affecting GSH, CoA, or protein synthesis rates.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C91 are supported by GOT1 KO/rescue experiments (Figure 6). Metabolomics data (C87-C88) demonstrate GOT1's role in sulfitolysis, while proliferation assays (C89) show GOT1-independent growth inhibition. Isotope tracing and protein synthesis assays (C91) rule out effects on major cysteine-dependent processes. The inference that intracellular metabolism contributes (C90) is reasonable given the GOT1-independent proliferation phenotype.

results.result: CDO1 expression depletes cellular NADPH (independent of GOT1), increases sensitivity to oxidative stress, impairs anchorage-independent growth, and inhibits NADPH-dependent metabolic processes including proline synthesis and reductive carboxylation, with these effects being cysteine-dependent.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C102 are well-supported by NADPH/NADP+ ratio measurements (C92-C93, Figure 7A), oxidative stress sensitivity assays (C94-C96, Figure 7C), soft agar assays (C97), and 13C5-glutamine tracing experiments (C98-C99, Figure 7D-F). The cysteine-dependence (C100-C101) is demonstrated by erastin treatment and low cystine rescue experiments (Figure 7 supplement 1D-F). The convergent evidence from multiple assays strongly supports the conclusion about NADPH depletion and its functional consequences.

results.result: In a KrasG12D; Trp53flox/flox lung tumor model, homozygous Keap1R554Q/R554Q mice show similar survival but develop lung hemorrhage, smaller tumors, strong Nrf2 activation, and Cdo1 accumulation compared to wild-type or heterozygous mice, suggesting Cdo1 may impede tumor progression.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C110 are partially supported by survival data (C103, Figure 8A), histology (C104, Figure 8B-C), tumor size quantification (C105-C106, Figure 8C), and immunohistochemistry (C107-C108, Figure 8D). However, the conclusion that Cdo1 impedes tumor progression (C110) is speculative. The smaller tumors in Keap1R554Q/R554Q mice could be due to Cdo1, but alternative explanations (other Keap1 substrates, Nrf2 effects) are not ruled out. The lung hemorrhage phenotype complicates interpretation of tumor burden. Additional work is explicitly stated as needed to establish causality.

results.result: High intracellular cysteine levels (often millimolar) are common in lung cancer cell lines including KEAP1 wild-type lines, suggesting NRF2-independent mechanisms promote cysteine uptake, and NRF2 stabilization promotes cysteine accumulation far exceeding levels necessary for cysteine-dependent processes.
results.evaluation: Claims C114-C115 and C125-C127 are supported by metabolomics data across the NSCLC cell line panel showing high cysteine in both NRF2HIGH and NRF2LOW lines (Figure 3D). The observation that millimolar cysteine accumulates without apparent toxicity (C127) is documented. The inference of NRF2-independent mechanisms (C115) is reasonable given high cysteine in KEAP1 wild-type lines. The comparison to normal ~100 μM levels (C126, cited) supports the conclusion of excessive accumulation (C125).

results.result: Cdo1 modestly limits GSH synthesis in MEFs (consistent with liver studies), but CDO1 depletes intracellular cysteine without limiting GSH synthesis in NSCLC cell lines, suggesting cancer cells are more efficient at maintaining cysteine/GSH levels, though this efficiency requires substantial NADPH consumption for continual cystine reduction.
results.evaluation: Claims C129-C134 are supported by experimental data comparing MEFs (Figure 2) and NSCLC cells (Figure 6D-G). The modest GSH limitation in MEFs (C129) is consistent with cited liver studies (C130). The lack of GSH limitation in NSCLC cells (C131) is demonstrated by isotope tracing. The speculation about cancer cell efficiency (C132) is reasonable given the data. The inference about NADPH consumption (C133-C134) is supported by comparison with published NADPH production rates and the observed NADPH depletion.

results.result: CSA is differentially metabolized in cancer cells versus MEFs, correlating with differential CSAD and GOT1 expression, with partitioning between decarboxylation (CSAD) and transamination (GOT1) likely influenced by enzyme levels and activities.
results.evaluation: Claims C135-C138 are supported by western blot analysis showing differential CSAD/GOT1 expression (Figure 5 supplement 2A, 3A) and metabolomics data showing different CSA metabolic fates in MEFs versus NSCLC cells. The established knowledge that CSAD has lower Km than GOT1 (C138) and that decarboxylation predominates at the organismal level (C137) provides mechanistic context. The inference about enzyme level influence (C136) is reasonable but appropriately labeled as not well-studied.

results.result: CDO1 promotes wasting of cysteine as CSA and sulfite, depletes cystine via sulfite, and induces NADPH depletion, demonstrating that oncogene-induced metabolic processes can be unfavorable.
results.evaluation: Claims C119-C121 and C124 summarize the major findings supported by the comprehensive experimental data throughout the manuscript. The characterization of these processes as "wasting" and "unfavorable" (C119, C124) is supported by the demonstrated toxicity, NADPH depletion, and growth inhibition. The conclusion about oncogene-induced processes being unfavorable (C124) is a reasonable inference from the data showing CDO1 as a liability in NRF2-activated cells.

results.result: Activating CDO1 expression may have unique therapeutic potential compared to cystine-depleting strategies, and Cdo1 accumulates in Keap1R554Q/R554Q tumors correlating with blocked tumor formation, though further work is needed to determine if Cdo1 impairs tumorigenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C149-C151 represent speculative therapeutic implications and future directions. While C150 is supported by the immunohistochemistry data (Figure 8D) showing Cdo1 accumulation and correlation with smaller tumors, the therapeutic potential (C149) is speculation based on the findings. C151 explicitly states that further work is needed to establish causality. These claims appropriately identify important questions but lack the experimental validation needed for full support.
